**[0:00] B1 · Buses and the Climate Card**
- two transit moves: the 2004 bus reform and the 2024 Climate Card

**[0:15] B2 · The 2004 bus reform**
- July 2004, switched in one night · center bus lanes, island stops, four route colors
- bus speed up to +11 km/h · main roads 33 to 50% faster (Dec 2004) · 24% fewer bus accidents, year one
- ridership up 9 to 21% depending on years compared (don't add them) · subsidies didn't come down at first

**[0:55] B3 · The Climate Card**
- ₩65,000 a month, unlimited · includes Ttareungi (tah-rung-ee) bikes
- not covered: Shinbundang Line, buses licensed outside Seoul, metropolitan express buses
- 10 million reloads by April 2025 · counts top-ups, so one rider can count many times · no user count or driving data

**[1:30] B4 · New York today**
- OMNY fare capping: rides free after a set number · Citi Bike separate
- similar idea to OMNY capping · Seoul adds bikes and a climate name

**[0:00] B1 · Five ideas for New York**
"So here are the five ideas I said New York could borrow from Seoul."

**[0:15] B2 · 01 Food waste by weight**
- NYC composting: 2.4% of home waste (2025), up from 1.4%
- fines April 2025, paused after 3 weeks, back Jan 1, 2026 · Independent Budget Office (IBO): pickup nearly tripled with fines, down about 43% after
- fix: bins that weigh food waste, in the building code (trash rooms already required)

**[0:50] B3 · 02 City retrofit loans (slow down)**
"This one is my main recommendation."
- Seoul: loans up to 100% of cost at 1.75%
- LL97 (over 25,000 sq ft): limits and fines · owners find the money
- about 11% of buildings over the 2024 to 2029 limits · about 63% over the 2030 limits if nothing changes

**[1:25] B4 · 03 Balcony solar kits**
- problems: code, permits, landlord consent
- asks: approved-kit list · simple DOB (Department of Buildings) permit · renter's right to install

**[1:55] B5 · 04 Climate transit pass**
- two asks: Citi Bike on the same OMNY pass, and a climate name · OMNY capping is similar (slide 18)

**[2:25] B6 · 05 Road removal**
- Cheonggyecheon: 168,000 vehicles a day · predicted gridlock never came
- NYC: BQE (Brooklyn-Queens Expressway), Cross Bronx cap (park deck over the sunken highway), Gowanus
- last 20 seconds: hold all five rows, move to the close
